The test image shows tomato leaves with numerous small dark brown/black spots scattered across the surface, some with lighter centers, along with slight yellowing around spots. Top candidates: Septoria Leaf Blotch, Bacterial Speck, Early Blight.

Now I'll view one reference from each top candidate class, then explore others.
Late Blight shows large necrotic patches. The test image has small discrete spots - pointing toward Septoria or Bacterial Speck. One more class to explore.

**Summary of observations:**

- **Test image**: Tomato compound leaf with many small, discrete dark brown/black spots scattered across leaflets. Some spots have slightly lighter centers. No large target rings, no coalesced patches, no white coating, no wilting.

- **Septoria CDDM_1928**: Small spots, circular, darker borders — pattern matches but different leaf type shown
- **Septoria CDDM_2685**: More advanced/coalesced dark patches — more severe than test
- **Bacterial Speck Bugwood_14/Bugwood_5**: Spots with yellow halos, somewhat larger and more angular
- **Early Blight**: Large concentric ring "target" spots — doesn't match
- **Late Blight**: Large brown necrotic patches — doesn't match
- **TSWV**: Whole-plant wilting — doesn't match
- **Alternaria**: Microscopic view only

**Conclusion**: The test image shows the classic presentation of Septoria Leaf Blotch — numerous small, round, dark-bordered spots scattered across tomato leaflets, some with lighter centers. This pattern is the hallmark of *Septoria lycopersici*. Bacterial Speck spots tend to have more prominent yellow halos and are typically more angular. The quantity and distribution of small discrete spots matches Septoria most closely.
